card.title: Frog — Habit, Habitat and External Features

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Rana tigrina is the model amphibian for NEB. It lives near water, spends most of the time on land, and returns to water to breed. External features include moist, glandular, scaleless skin; a tympanum; a nictitating membrane; 4-digit forelimbs; and 5-digit webbed hindlimbs. The tadpole has a tail and gills; the adult loses the tail and gains lungs.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
External: head (eyes, tympanum, nostrils) + neck + trunk + 4 limbs (forelimb 4 digits, hindlimb 5 digits, webbed)
Adaptations: moist skin, webbed feet, sticky pads, tympanum, nictitating membrane
Metamorphosis: tadpole (tail + gills) → adult frog (no tail + lungs)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Frogs are amphibians, NOT reptiles; they need moist skin and return to water to breed.  ·  Adult frogs have NO tail; tadpoles (larvae) have a tail (metamorphosis).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects a labelled external diagram of the frog.  ·  The digit count (4 fore, 5 hind) is a very common exam detail.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Webbed hind feet: for swimming (amphibious life).  ·  Sticky pads on forelimbs: for climbing surfaces.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Forelimbs have 4 digits; hindlimbs have 5 digits (webbed) — a key exam point.  ·  The tympanum is the external ear (eardrum); the nictitating membrane is a transparent third eyelid.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Label external frog  ·  Explain habitat and habits

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Frog digits: 4 fore + 5 hind (webbed).  ·  Amphibian = amphi (both) + bios (life) = land + water.

rows.text: Amphibian body plan  ·  External features (tympanum, nictitating membrane)  ·  Digit count (4 + 5)  ·  Moist glandular skin

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Rana tigrina: amphibian, ~5–8 cm, lives near water.  ·  External: moist glandular skin, 4 forelimb digits, 5 webbed hindlimb digits.  ·  Tympanum (eardrum) + nictitating membrane (third eyelid).  ·  No tail in adults; tadpole has a tail (metamorphosis).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Rana tigrina has 4 forelimb digits and 5 webbed hindlimb digits.  ·  The frog tadpole has a tail and gills; the adult loses the tail and gains lungs.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Differentiate the forelimbs and hindlimbs of a frog.  ·  State the adaptations of the frog to an amphibious life.  ·  State the taxonomic position of Rana tigrina.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: State the adaptations to amphibious life.  ·  Explain metamorphosis (tadpole → frog).

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Moist, glandular skin: for cutaneous respiration and protection.  ·  Tympanum (eardrum): for hearing; nictitating membrane: for eye protection underwater.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: The frog's hindlimbs have how many digits? → B  ·  The external eardrum of a frog is called: → A

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Rana tigrina (tiger frog / Indian frog): amphibian; ~5–8 cm long; model organism for NEB.  ·  Habit and habitat: lives near water (ponds, streams, wetlands); spends most of the time on land but returns to water for breeding.  ·  External features: moist, glandular, scaleless skin (cutaneous respiration); four limbs (forelimbs 4 digits, hindlimbs 5 digits, webbed); tympanum (eardrum); nictitating membrane (third eyelid); lateral line absent in adults.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Metamorphosis  ·  Adaptations to amphibious life  ·  Taxonomy (Anura)

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Adaptations: webbed feet (swimming), sticky pads (climbing), moist skin (respiration).  ·  Taxonomy: Amphibia > Anura > Rana.  ·  Cutaneous respiration is significant in addition to lungs.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Frogs do NOT have a lateral line in adulthood (it is present in tadpoles).  ·  Cutaneous respiration (skin) is major in frogs; lungs are also present but the skin contributes significantly to gas exchange.  ·  Metamorphosis (tadpole → frog) is a frequent topic.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Adaptations to amphibious life (skin, feet, tympanum) are a favourite application question.  ·  Memorise the digit count (4 fore, 5 hind).  ·  Learn the external features (tympanum, nictitating membrane, skin).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: List adaptations to amphibious life.  ·  Rana tigrina is an amphibian that lives near water but spends most of the time on land.  ·  The frog has 4 forelimb digits and 5 webbed hindlimb digits.
